message.content:
The most well‑known dominant genetic trait in lions is the **presence of a mane in adult males**.  
In male lions, a specific set of genes (including those that regulate androgen receptors and hair follicle growth) are expressed in a dominant fashion, leading to the development of the thick, dark mane that distinguishes them from females and from other big‑cat species.
